subject.title: fix embedded compaction hook reset API

question: Should OpenClaw support a current-session-only `resetSession(reason?)` capability specifically on successful `after_compaction` hook contexts?
rationale: This is a new compatibility-sensitive plugin capability that can archive session state; code review can narrow the implementation, but cannot establish the permanent public hook contract without owner intent.

options.title: Approve after-compaction-only API
options.body: Support the capability only on successful `after_compaction` contexts, with outer-lifecycle deferral, focused contract tests, and real reset proof.

options.title: Approve a broader hook API
options.body: Intentionally expose session reset to additional hook phases, then document and test exactly which phases may reset sessions and when queued requests flush.

options.title: Keep reset owner-internal
options.body: Reject the plugin-facing API and require compaction owners or a narrower plugin-owned integration to request session rotation through an internal seam.

recommendation.title: Approve after-compaction-only API
recommendation.body: Support the capability only on successful `after_compaction` contexts, with outer-lifecycle deferral, focused contract tests, and real reset proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They are connected to both the original compaction/reset hook work and subsequent plugin-hook architecture changes.
